To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the changes in the percentages in the subpopulations of CD56+ lymphocyte subsets in peripheral blood are associated with the response and disease progression in patients with metastasis colorectal cancer.

the changes in the percentages in the amounts of peripheral white blood cells, particularly in the amounts of CD16+, or CD56+ lymphocyte subsets, are associated with the response of metastatic colorectal patients to treatment with cetuxmab-based regimens.
the assessment of immune cell subsets in patients with metastasis before the initiation of cetuximab therapy may provide valuable information about the response to treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential clinical significance of the assessment of the percentages of peripheral white blood cells in patients with metastases of colorectal cancer.
a potential clinical relevance of the peripheral white blood cell subsets assessment in the context of metastatic colorectal carcinoma treated with cetuximabbased regimens.
the changes in the percentages and proportions of immune cells in patients with metastases of colorectal cancer before and 2 months following the treatment with cetixumab.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the changes of peripheral immune cell percentages before treatment initiation may have a prognostic value in metastatic colorectal patients.
the assessment of immune cell subsets before treatment may provide additional information for the selection of the optimal treatment strategy in patients with colorectal cancer.

the assessment of the percentages of CD3-, CD56+, and/or CD16+ cells in the peripheral blood may be a promising tool in the prediction of the response to treatment in patients with metastases of wild-type KRAS colorectal cancer treated with cetuximabad-based regimens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we observed a significant decrease in percentages of CD16+ and CD56+ lymphocyte subsets in patients with metastastic colorectal cancer compared to healthy individuals.

the changes in the amounts and percentages of peripheral blood cells in patients with metastasis of colorectal cancer may serve as a potential prognostic factor for the response to therapy with cetuximabbased regimens, especially when combined with the assessment of KRAS mutations.

the changes in the percentage of CD56+ lymphocyte subsets in the overall white cell pool in patients with metastasis before the treatment initiation may be a prognostic factor for the response to cetuximab therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the evaluation of the percentage of circulating immune cells before treatment initiation and after 2 months of treatment in patients with metastastic colorectal cancer may be clinically relevant, as it may be used for the prediction of the response to treatment.

the changes in the percentages and the ratio of peripheral immune cells in the white blood cell pool before treatment initiation may serve as an additional prognostic factor in patients with metastasis colorectal cancer.
peripheral blood analysis can be used as a prognostic marker for patients with metastatic CRC.
